cheat.title: The Unit 2 pattern
items: New and improved tools (credit, caravanserai, compass, saddles) → more trade → bigger cities and states → cultural and environmental effects.
Contextualization sentence: "After 1200, existing trade routes across Afro-Eurasia intensified as stable states, especially the Mongols, protected merchants and new technologies made travel easier."

cheat.title: Dates to know
items: 1235: Sundiata founds Mali.  1240: Golden Horde destroys Kiev.
1258: Hulegu takes Baghdad.  1271: Kublai founds the Yuan.
c. 1250–1350: Pax Mongolica.  1324: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage.
1347–1351: Black Death in Europe.  1368: Ming replace the Yuan.
1405–1433: Zheng He's seven voyages.  1453: Ottomans take Constantinople.

cheat.title: Effects in one line each
items: Religion: spread by merchants and rulers, often blending (syncretism): Chan, Neo-Confucianism, Angkor, Swahili, Urdu.
Technology: gunpowder and papermaking moved west; Islamic scholars saved Greek works and added Indian math.
Crops: Champa rice (China), bananas (Africa), citrus, sugar and cotton → population growth.
Environment: overgrazing, deforestation, erosion (Great Zimbabwe abandoned).
Disease: plague rode the trade routes → labor shortage → higher wages → feudalism weakened.

cheat.title: Travelers' points of view
items: Marco Polo: Venetian merchant (trade and cities).
Ibn Battuta: Moroccan Muslim scholar (mostly Muslim lands).
Margery Kempe: English Christian pilgrim (a middle-class woman's life).
